chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said:
The Imamate does not come together in two brothers after al-Hasan and al-Husayn. Rather, it is among the descendants and the descendants of the descendants.

key_terms.أَخَوَيْنِ: two brothers; indicating that the Imamate does not continue in sibling succession after the stated exception
key_terms.أَعْقَابِ الْأَعْقَابِ: the descendants of the descendants; later generations of progeny
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةُ: the divinely designated leadership and authority of the Imam
key_terms.بَعْدَ: after; marking the point following al-Hasan and al-Husayn عليهما السلام

ai.seo_question: Does the Imamate continue in two brothers after al-Hasan and al-Husayn عليهما السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that after al-Hasan and al-Husayn عليهما السلام, the Imamate does not continue in two brothers simultaneously or successively as brothers. Rather, it continues through lineal descendants, establishing hereditary succession within the designated progeny.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary, from Hammad Bin Isa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Imamate will not gather to be in two brothers after Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. But rather, it would be in the descendants and descendants of the descendants’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al Husayn from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from Sulayman ibn Ja‘fari from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) does not take place in two brothers after al-Hassan and al-Husayn (a.s.). It only continues in the descendents of the Imam (a.s.) generation after the generation.”
